title: Construction Tendering: Why You Keep Losing Bids
meta_description: Why construction tendering fails: seven root causes that lose bids before the price is even checked, and the fixes that lift your strike rate.
h1: Construction Tendering: Why You Keep Losing Bids
hero_subtitle: A practical guide to finding where your bids leak value before a contract is signed.

intro.answer: If your team works flat out and still wins fewer than half its tenders, the problem is not price. Entire bids fail on small technical errors before anyone checks the number.

image.alt: A construction tender being prepared against a deadline

intro.roadmap: This guide covers the hidden cost of poor tendering, a symptom checker for whether you are bleeding bids, the seven root causes that derail the process, and the fixes that lift a strike rate without joining a race to the bottom.

briefing.title: Run Tendering as a Task, Not a Scramble
briefing.intro: Most builders land only 40 to 50% of the bids they enter. The best organised reach 65% or more, and they are not winning because they are cheaper. They are winning because the process is deliberate rather than a last-minute rush of paperwork.

panels.heading: Why do tenders fail even with a keen price?
paragraphs: Because most failures happen before the price is read. A vague scope, assumptions nobody wrote down, an incomplete PQQ, or an estimate that was rushed and out of date will end a bid on its own.
Then there is what gets ignored: social value and ESG are scored, and leaving them thin costs marks that price cannot buy back.

panels.heading: The seven root causes to check
paragraphs: Work down this list against your last five bids and the pattern usually shows itself quickly.
steps: Rushed or out of date estimates.
No post-bid debrief loop, so nothing is learned.

review.label: The measure
review.text: Track your strike rate honestly, bid by bid, with the reason for each loss. Without that number you are guessing at whether anything you change is working.
